 ‘Fraud factory’ stole $7 million in SNAP benefits to fund luxury cars, global payments
 By Barbara Russo-Lennon 
 … Comments 
 Posted on October 30, 2026 
 Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg Photo by Dean Moses 
 Eight people were indicted in connection with an alleged scheme to steal more than $7 million in Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits from April 2023 through September 2025, Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg and Department of Investigation Commissioner Nadia Shihata announced on Thursday.   
 The millions were then used to buy a string of luxury vehicles and send tens of thousands of dollars to Yemen and other locations around the world.   
 The district attorney’s office released some of the defendants’ names on Oct. 29, which include Belal Hauter, 34, Gregory Fabiani, 46, Abdulla Aezah, 35, Milton Rios, 53, and Yvette Rivera, 58, all of whom were charged in a NYS Supreme Court indictment with fourth-degree conspiracy and various counts of grand larceny and identity theft.
 The alleged scheme affected thousands of SNAP recipients, some of whom never received reimbursement for their stolen benefits, prosecutors said.   
 “SNAP and EBT fraud harms New Yorkers in need of assistance and the New Yorkers whose tax dollars fund these essential programs,” Bragg said.
 Fraud factory in a Yonkers deli
 Photographic evidence obtained in the case showed members of the conspiracy operating what was essentially a fraud factory from the back room of a Yonkers deli and from hotels, prosecutors allege.
 Images of Alleged EBT Fraud Operation Seized through Court-Authorized Warrant 
 According to court documents, the defendants allegedly used the names of existing or made-up delis, bodegas and grocery stores to establish merchant processing accounts and obtain point-of-sale (POS) systems capable of handling Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) transactions.
 Investigators allege that the group used stolen EBT account numbers and PINs, many obtained through card-skimming devices, to create duplicate cards. The defendants allegedly monitored when the benefits were put into the compromised accounts and used the cloned cards to withdraw the funds through repeated transactions.
 In some cases, legitimate benefit recipients attempted to purchase food and other necessities on the same day their benefits were deposited, only to discover their accounts had already been drained, prosecutors said
 “The defendants allegedly tracked the timing of benefit funds and drained accounts before the legitimate SNAP recipient could buy food and other necessities, eventually stealing more than $7 million,” Bragg explained.
 Prosecutors allege that Hauter led the operation by opening or directing others to open numerous merchant processing accounts in the names of various food businesses. Members of the group also allegedly established bank accounts connected to the processing accounts so the money from fraudulent transactions would flow into accounts they controlled.
 Fabiani and Aezah allegedly helped make the accounts and provided tech support for the processing systems and POS machines. Other defendants allegedly used the machines to conduct thousands of transactions.
 Rios and Rivera allegedly opened additional merchant processing and bank accounts as part of the scheme.
 The stolen funds allegedly were used to purchase multiple luxury vehicles and to send tens of thousands of dollars to Yemen and elsewhere internationally, prosecutors said.
